facts.fact: The Banque Centrale du Congo launched its new website on 14 August 2026, on which the public can consult exchange rates, inflation, interest rates, statistics and economic indicators, and publications; the document does not say the data can be downloaded or give a licence.

The Institut National de la Statistique (INS), the national statistics office, officially launched data.gouv.cd on 2026-02-23, described as the national open data platform of the DRC and framed as part of the Government's vision for transparency; the document names no open data policy, strategy or decree behind it, so it does not tie the portal to a policy.

The INS releases datasets on data.gouv.cd covering demography, economy, health, education, public finance, agriculture and infrastructure in CSV, XLSX and JSON; the document gives no count of datasets or of publishing bodies and names no ministry other than the INS.

facts.fact: ITIE-RDC, the DR Congo's extractive industries transparency body, publishes extractive revenue, mining production, mining-rights and contract datasets for download in CSV, Excel and JSON, with a public API.
The national statistics institute INS of the DR Congo runs a statistical portal offering 15 searchable indicators that users can explore and export, the newest dated February 2026.
Pollicy says the DRC open data portal, supported by the AfDB's Open Data for Africa with contributions from the National Statistics Institute, has not been updated recently.
The DRC Ministry of Mines publishes validated mining statistics files for 2017 to 2025 on its statistics page, each stated to be open-access and downloadable, with no licence named.
